newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Gaddum sees German rates steady in nearterm.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Gaddum sees German rates steady in nearterm.

text.p: German interest rates are likely to remain unchanged for the foreseeable future as there is currently no reason to either raise or lower them, Bundesbank deputy president Johann Wilhelm Gaddum said.

"In Germany there are no signals that a raising of rates will be necessary in the forseeable future," Gaddum told a news agency in an interview published on Monday. A Bundesbank spokesman confirmed the comments on Tuesday.
Gaddum also said, "unless you have a decent reason for a change, you should let it be."

Since the Bundesbank unexpectedly cut its main money market rate by 30 basis points to three percent in late August, several Bundesbank council members have said that there was now little immediate need to adjust policy again.

The Bundesbank's key policy indicator M3 money supply continues to grow at a rate above the four to seven percent target growth corridor. In August, M3 expanded at an annualised rate of 8.7 percent, up from 8.6 percent in July.
The German discount rate is a 2.50 percent while the emergency Lombard borrowing rate is at 4.50 percent.
